low-redundancy textual memory framework Mem0. The results indicate that in Mem0, which has relatively low

positive_signals: MemForest is a general agent memory compression framework that partitions historical memory into event-centric EventTrees using global semantic similarity and local temporal continuity, then progressively merges nodes within each EventTree.
The Anchor-Guided Propagation Retrieval (AGPR) mechanism retrieves additional relevant memory nodes from temporal neighborhoods of key memory nodes to improve retrieval accuracy.

The paper provides a theoretical analysis showing that merging highly similar memory nodes preserves higher query similarity, with a lower bound on merged-node query similarity that increases monotonically with node similarity.

The paper positions MemForest against existing memory compression and token compression work, noting that prior post-processing compression is restricted to graph-structured streaming video scenarios and that token compression methods overlook event differentiation and temporal relationships.
The paper acknowledges that performance degradation becomes pronounced at higher compression rates in the low-redundancy Mem0 framework, with accuracy dropping to 93.3% at 70% compression.
